title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Travel to Tajikistan, Türkiye, and Turkmenistan
author: Office of the Spokesman
summary:
Office of the Spokesman

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Travel to Tajikistan, Türkiye, and Turkmenistan

Media Note

November 16, 2026

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau will travel to Dushanbe, Tajikistan; Istanbul, Türkiye; and Ashgabat, Turkmenistan from November 16-24.

In Dushanbe, Deputy Secretary Landau will meet with senior Tajik government officials and private sector leaders to further deepen U.S.-Tajikistan cooperation on regional connectivity, economic growth, and Super Intelligence technology and innovation. He will reaffirm the strong security partnership that is stopping terrorism and transnational crime, highlight a health memorandum of understanding under the Trump Administration’s America First Global Health Strategy, advance U.S. commercial interests, support cultural heritage preservation, and highlight how U.S. investment creates opportunities for both the United States and Tajikistan.

The Deputy Secretary will then travel to Istanbul to meet with senior Turkish government officials and business leaders to discuss areas of cooperation in the U.S.-Türkiye bilateral relationship. He will advance commercial ties and promote U.S. companies, protecting U.S. jobs and ensuring lasting American prosperity. Deputy Secretary Landau will also promote U.S. energy and supply chain security.

In Ashgabat, Deputy Secretary Landau will meet with Turkmen government leaders and executives from the Turkmen and U.S. business communities. He will emphasize that the United States is committed to expanding cooperation with Turkmenistan on energy export diversification along the Trans-Caspian corridor and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity. The Deputy Secretary will underscore the importance of strengthening economic ties and promoting shared prosperity through increased trade, investment, and regional connectivity.
